title: Oman and Saudi Arabia Face Off in Gulf 27 Without Two Key Players
seoTitle: Oman vs Saudi Arabia in Gulf 27: Key Players Out
subtitle: Saudi and Omani Teams Take the Field at Al-Inma with Significant Lineup Doubts
excerpt: In Gulf Cup 27's second round, Saudi Arabia faces Oman without Mohammed Al-Qahtani and Nawaf Al-Aqidi. Moroccan coach Tarek Sektioui seeks a crucial win.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Oman and Saudi Arabia, scheduled for this Saturday at Al-Inma Stadium, has garnered attention because both teams approach the match with absences that could change the course of the Gulf 27 group stage.

Saudi National Team Absentees

Saudi Arabia confirmed that Mohammed Al-Qahtani, Al-Qadsiah forward, experienced abdominal pain and did not participate in the last training session, ruling him out of the match against Oman. Al-Qahtani had not played since the 1-0 victory over Kuwait, when he came on as a substitute for a few minutes.

In addition, goalkeeper Nawaf Al-Aqidi was excluded from the official list after an elbow injury in the same match against Kuwait. The official statement released on the X network informed that the medical report confirmed he was unfit to play and required treatment and rehabilitation.

With Al-Aqidi out, Mohammed Al-Owais of Al-Hilal is expected to take the starting position between the posts, while Abdulqadous Atiyah of Al-Ula was called up to cover the absence.

Oman Seeks Victory to Maintain Hope

Moroccan coach Tarek Sektioui stated in the press conference that the match is “difficult for both sides” and that the Omani team enters with the mentality of “there is no alternative but victory.” The coach emphasized the importance of technical and physical preparation and assured that no player has a worrying injury.

Abdulmajid Al-Balushi, a young player for the Oman national team, reinforced the objective of securing three points and accumulating the necessary results to advance in the competition.

What's at Stake in the Group Stage

Saudi Arabia needs a positive result against Oman to guarantee qualification for the semifinals, regardless of what happens in the match against Iraq in the third round. Oman, on the other hand, needs to win its next two matches to keep its chances of advancing alive.

Expectations for the Clash

According to Sektioui, the strength of the Saudi national team lies in the support of the local crowd, but the Omani team relies on “fighting spirit” and “personality” to face the opponent. Saudi coach Georgios Donis has not yet released the final lineup, but the absence of Al-Qahtani and Al-Aqidi indicates that the coach will have to adjust the offensive scheme and defensive security.

Impact on the Tournament

The result of this encounter could define the qualification of both teams. A Saudi victory would secure a spot in the semifinals, while an Oman victory would put pressure on Saudi Arabia in the upcoming matches and pave the way for a possible surprise later in Gulf 27.
